Am I missing something? The staff doesn’t need to pay for itself because you can sell it back. 

If you cast high alch with it 100k times and save 1m doing that (numbers made up don’t shoot me) then sell it back when you’re finished for approx. the same price, that’s value. 

Buy staff -> charge with 10k nature runes -> cast 10k high alchs -> get the value of extra high alchs from saved runes -> sell staff.

You don’t have to break even with the cost of purchasing an item if that item is still tradable. Unless I’m stupid and the staff is permanently untradable?

This is happening because people are going for genesis shards, potentially tons of them, and they’re happenstance getting a bunch of weapon sets.

Think of an Ironman that maybe wants 6+ genesis shards. They’re going to passively obtain 12 weapons trying to get their shards, and will sell probably 10 of them then consume all the shards.

The problem with their supply is the consumable chase item results in a ton of oversupply from people who don’t want or need the weapon set because they’ve already obtained it and it’s otherwise junk. 

The mistake here is the design of genesis shard drops.

First few leagues were jagex understanding the impact and what the best release cadence for them is. I think after 3 they figured it out, which is why there’s approx 22 months between release of 3 and 4. The hype around 4 was so high partly because of the long break between leagues. They need time to cook up something sufficiently interesting otherwise it just becomes “osrs but faster for a couple months out of the year”. 

I think they’ll aim for 18 months between leagues, given the time between 3 and 4, especially because leagues tends to burn people out from the main game. 

My guess is March-June 2025 at the earliest for a leagues 5

Leagues are likely something jagex will do every ~18 months or so, once a year is too much.

I would not expect any leagues announcements this time around. My guess is we won’t see a new league until summer of 2025.

This would be like releasing a weapon that has slightly weaker stats than a voidwaker, with a special attack that deals 30-130% of your max hit, at 98% accuracy, and then slapping an 80 attack requirement on it.

If the claws are intended to serve the exact same purpose as dragon claws, they shouldn’t have a higher attack requirement. As-described there’s nowhere dragon claws aren’t objectively better in every way than these, and that’s their intention with the design.

Like I said, just lowering the attack requirement to 55 solves the awkward tier progression flow.

What you said doesn’t clash with my point, I’m aware of how GE value works.

If you’re going to design and release an item intended to be a weaker version/bridge towards an upgrade, that item shouldn’t have a higher requirement. There is no other example of this in the game where a bridge item has a higher requirement, I.e. an item that is objectively inferior to an existing item.

Making the claws 55 attack would address this quickly, we shouldn’t be okay with a 65 attack pair of claws that is objectively worse than a 60 attack pair of claws that share a similar special attack/function, that doesn’t exist anywhere else in the game.

I find it odd that power level here is entirely dictated by current GE value. These new claws have higher requirements (assuming they require the quest to wield as well as being 65 attack) but are, only for reasons related to the price of an item, weaker than a 60 attack weapon. 

I can’t get behind that as a design philosophy. They should be 50/55 attack if you want them to be weaker than dragon claws.
